title: Return to the land of promise
summary: The Lord shows mercy to Jacob and chooses Israel; strangers join the house of Jacob. The people return to their lands of promise, and Israel rules over its oppressors.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, choose Israel, and set them in their own land.
Strangers will join and cleave to the house of Jacob.
The people will return from far away to their lands of promise, and the house of Israel will rule over their oppressors.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic depiction of returning people and a land of promise.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities beyond the text’s collective labels, clothing, architecture, and terrain.

narration.text: the strangers shall be joined with them
they shall return to their lands of promise

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Prophetic future events are conveyed as a vision or symbolic tableau, not as a specified historical present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord’s appearance; none is described.
Do not identify the returnees or strangers beyond the text.

title: Rest from bondage
summary: The Lord gives the addressed people rest from sorrow, fear, and hard bondage.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will give the addressed people rest from sorrow, fear, and hard bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained symbolic image of people at rest.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities, appearance, and setting.

narration.text: the Lord shall give thee rest

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a promised future, not a narrated present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure; no appearance is stated.

title: Proverb against Babylon’s king
summary: The people take up a proverb against Babylon’s king, declaring the oppressor ended and the rulers’ scepters broken.

explicit_facts.text: The addressed people will take up a proverb against the king of Babylon.
The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked and the scepters of rulers.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic visual of broken royal emblems may accompany off-screen recitation.
unspecified_visual_details: The king’s appearance, the speakers’ identities, and the setting.

narration.text: How hath the oppressor ceased, the golden city ceased!
The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The proverb is reported speech; the visual should not invent a specific performance or audience.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a named or identifiable Babylonian king.

title: The oppressor brought low
summary: The one who ruled nations in anger is persecuted. The whole earth is quiet and breaks into singing.

explicit_facts.text: The former oppressor is persecuted, and none hinders.
The whole earth is at rest and quiet; they break forth into singing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic, broad view of a quiet earth, with singing conveyed off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the oppressor and singers.

narration.text: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet
they break forth into singing.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statement that the oppressor is persecuted is not elaborated into a specific combat event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a pursuer, battle, or oppressor’s identity.

title: The trees rejoice
summary: The fir-trees and cedars of Lebanon are personified as rejoicing that no feller comes against them.

explicit_facts.text: The fir-trees and cedars of Lebanon rejoice, saying no feller comes against them after the oppressor is laid down.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A landscape with fir-trees and cedars; their rejoicing is figurative.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise landscape and any visual personification.

narration.text: Since thou art laid down no feller is come up against us.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees’ speech is personification, not evidence of literal talking trees.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict trees with human faces or bodies as literal beings.

title: The dead meet the fallen king
summary: Hell stirs the dead and the kings of nations from their thrones to meet the fallen king; they ask whether he has become weak like them.

explicit_facts.text: Hell from beneath is moved to meet the king; the dead and kings of nations are raised from their thrones.
They ask whether he has become weak and like them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic underworld gathering of dead kings.
unspecified_visual_details: The dead kings’ appearance, the underworld’s appearance, and the fallen king’s identity or appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Art thou also become weak as we?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The dead kings

spoken_dialogue.text: Art thou become like unto us?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The dead kings

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage uses prophetic and poetic imagery; avoid asserting a specific geography or mechanics of the afterlife.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the kings or depict the fallen king beyond what is stated.

title: Pomp brought to the grave
summary: The king’s pomp is brought down to the grave, his viols are silent, and worms cover him.

explicit_facts.text: The king’s pomp is brought down to the grave; the noise of his viols is not heard, and worms cover him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic grave scene with a silent instrument and worms.
unspecified_visual_details: The king’s visible appearance, the instrument’s design, and the grave’s form.

narration.text: Thy pomp is brought down to the grave
the noise of thy viols is not heard

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The figure is addressed as the fallen king; no name is given here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show gore, exposed wounds, or a detailed corpse.

title: Poetic Address to Lucifer
summary: The poetic passage addresses Lucifer as fallen from heaven and cut down to the ground, and reports inward aspirations to ascend, exalt his throne, sit upon the mount of the congregation, and be like the Most High.

explicit_facts.text: The passage addresses Lucifer as son of the morning, fallen from heaven, cut down to the ground, and one who weakened the nations.

The poetic address attributes inward words to Lucifer about ascending into heaven, exalting his throne above the stars of God, and sitting upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north.
The reported inward words continue with aspirations to ascend above the clouds and be like the Most High.

unspecified_visual_details: No physical staging, visible appearances, or present location is supplied.
Typography and a nonrepresentational background for presenting the passage are creative design choices.

narration.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!
For thou hast said in thy heart:
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the narrator under the supplied narrator identification; this does not establish his visible presence or a face-to-face encounter.
Lucifer is addressed within poetry, not established as a physically present character.
The inward words are reported through narration, not presented as audible dialogue.
Heaven, stars, the throne, the mount, and clouds belong to the poetic address and inward aspirations, not an established visible setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an encounter between Nephi and Lucifer.
Do not depict the poetic fall or cutting down as a newly occurring visible event.
Do not depict the proposed ascent, enthronement, or likeness to the Most High as accomplished events.
Do not invent visible appearances for Lucifer, God, or the Most High.
Do not turn inward words into audible speech.

title: Brought down to the pit
summary: The fallen one is brought down to the pit. Those who see him consider him and ask whether he was the one who shook kingdoms and made the world a wilderness.

explicit_facts.text: The addressed one will be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.
Those who see him look closely and ask whether he made the earth tremble and shook kingdoms.
They also ask whether he made the world a wilderness, destroyed its cities, and did not open the house of his prisoners.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Observers may be shown looking toward an unnamed fallen figure; the destruction is referenced rather than replayed.
unspecified_visual_details: The observers, the figure’s appearance, and the pit’s appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Those who see him

spoken_dialogue.text: And made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof, and opened not the house of his prisoners?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Those who see him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The observers’ question recalls past deeds; do not depict those deeds as a current scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add named witnesses or show the past destruction as happening now.

title: The dishonored burial
summary: The kings of nations lie in glory in their own houses, unlike the addressed king, who is cast out of his grave and not joined with them in burial.

explicit_facts.text: All the kings of nations lie in glory, each in his own house.
The addressed king is cast out of his grave like an abominable branch, among those slain, and is compared to a carcass trodden underfoot.
He will not be joined with them in burial because he destroyed his land and slew his people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A contrast between dignified burial places and an excluded grave may be represented symbolically.
unspecified_visual_details: The houses, graves, kings’ appearances, and precise manner of exclusion.

narration.text: All the kings of the nations, yea, all of them, lie in glory
Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Past death and burial are described poetically; this is not a new combat scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore, wounds, or identifiable slain people.

title: Babylon’s destruction foretold
summary: Slaughter is prepared for the evildoer’s children; the Lord declares that Babylon’s name and remnant will be cut off and the land made a possession for the bittern and pools of water.

explicit_facts.text: Slaughter is to be prepared for the children of the evildoer because of their fathers’ iniquities, so they do not rise, possess the land, or fill the world with cities.
The Lord of Hosts says he will cut off from Babylon the name, remnant, son, and nephew.
The Lord will make it a possession for the bittern and pools of water and sweep it with destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An abandoned, waterlogged Babylon may be shown symbolically; the threatened slaughter need not be depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s architecture, the bird’s appearance, and the manner or timing of destruction.

narration.text: I will also make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic declaration, not a present-tense destruction scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the slaughter of children.
Do not invent a named attacker or specific destructive event.

title: The Lord’s purpose stands
summary: The Lord of Hosts swears that his purpose will stand, declares that the Assyrian will be brought into his land and trodden underfoot on his mountains, and affirms that no one can disannul or turn back his purpose.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord of Hosts swears that what he has thought and purposed will come to pass and stand.
The Lord will bring the Assyrian into his land and tread him underfoot on his mountains; the yoke and burden will depart from the people.
This purpose is upon the whole earth, and the Lord’s hand is stretched out upon all nations.
No one can disannul the Lord’s purpose or turn back his hand.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic image of a burden lifted may accompany the spoken prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s appearance, the Assyrian’s appearance, the mountains, and the people freed from the burden.

narration.text: Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass
and as I have purposed, so shall it stand—
his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s first-person declaration is quoted as narration; no visible divine figure is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord bodily or invent an appearance.
Do not turn the prophecy into a specific battle scene.

title: The burden concerning Palestina
summary: The burden is dated to the year King Ahaz died. Palestina is warned not to rejoice: a cockatrice and fiery flying serpent will come from the serpent’s root; the poor will feed and lie safely, famine will strike the root, and smoke will come from the north.

explicit_facts.text: The burden was in the year King Ahaz died.
Palestina is told not to rejoice because a cockatrice and fiery flying serpent will come from the serpent’s root.
The first-born of the poor will feed and the needy lie safely; famine will kill the addressed root and a remnant will be slain.
The gate and city are told to howl and cry; smoke will come from the north.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The serpent imagery may be rendered symbolically; the smoke may be a distant omen.
unspecified_visual_details: The creatures’ appearance, the city’s appearance, the people’s identities, and the source or nature of the smoke.

narration.text: the needy shall lie down in safety
there shall come from the north a smoke

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Serpent language is figurative prophecy unless represented explicitly as such; do not make it a literal supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the promised famine or slaying as a present event.
Do not invent the serpent creatures’ designs or identify a specific invading force.

title: Messengers answer the nations
summary: The messengers of the nations are asked what answer they will give: the Lord has founded Zion, and the poor of his people will trust in it.

explicit_facts.text: The messengers of the nations are asked what they will answer.
The answer is that the Lord has founded Zion and the poor of his people will trust in it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic view of Zion may accompany the reported answer.
unspecified_visual_details: The messengers’ identities, number, appearance, and Zion’s appearance.

narration.text: the Lord hath founded Zion
the poor of his people shall trust in it.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The messengers and answer are reported in a prophetic question; do not invent an exchange or specific people.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord’s appearance or invent the messengers’ identities.
